chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, who said:
I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about vomiting, nosebleeding, and pus: do they invalidate wudu (ablution) or not? He said: They do not invalidate anything.

As for what Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated in the report that we mentioned in the chapter before this, from his statement: If the blood is forced out, it invalidates, and if it is not forced out, it does not invalidate.

key_terms.اسْتُكْرِهَ: was forced out or made to come out
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Do vomiting, nosebleeding, or pus invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that vomiting, nosebleeding, and pus do not invalidate wudu (ablution). It also references another report concerning blood being forced out, indicating a juristic discussion about how such narrations are to be understood together.
